featured.reason: Official Chrome DevTools MCP server, CLI and skills (Apache-2.0) that let coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and Gemini control and inspect a live Chrome browser for reliable automation, in-depth debugging and performance analysis. A Claude Code plugin installs the MCP server and all skills (chrome-devtools, chrome-devtools-cli, a11y-debugging, cookie-debugging, debug-optimize-lcp, memory-leak-debugging, troubleshooting). Rated 5. Caveats: usage statistics are enabled by default (opt out with `--no-usage-statistics` or CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_USAGE_STATISTICS); requires Node.js LTS and current Google Chrome; the MCP client can see browser content. Archive completeness: tracked source and the pinned direct submodule third_party/devtools-frontend @ ab6a630 were verified; 7 nested optional submodules of devtools-frontend (llvm-project and Chromium build tooling) were not fetched because the parent .gitmodules sets fetchRecurseSubmodules=false.
ideas: Install the official Claude Code plugin (`/plugin marketplace add ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`, then `/plugin install chrome-devtools-mcp@chrome-devtools-plugins`) with `--no-usage-statistics`, and have the agent open the live ai-daily-radar GitHub Pages site and record a performance trace (INP, LCP) at a mobile viewport to check the animated background.
Use the a11y-debugging skill on the site's Chinese/English language switch and filter controls so the agent reports accessibility issues from a live Chrome session, not guesses from the HTML.
Point the agent at a failing UI change and have it use the network and console tools (source-mapped stacks) to find the regression, then apply the fix.
Use the CLI (`chrome-devtools navigate_page` / `take_screenshot`) in a headless script after each site publish to keep a visual regression log.
Follow the Advanced Usage guide to connect to Chrome on the Android phone for on-device debugging of the WebView app, or run the MCP as a browser subagent alongside Claude Code or Codex.

featured.reason: Alibaba's Open Code Review CLI (Apache-2.0), battle-tested internally: a hybrid of deterministic review pipelines and an LLM agent that writes precise line-level comments, with official plugins/skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code and OpenCode, plus an MCP server and a delegation mode that uses the host agent's model (no separate OCR API key). Rated 5. Caveat: default `ocr review` needs a configured OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible model endpoint; the published benchmark trades some recall for higher precision and about 1/9 the tokens of a general-purpose agent.
ideas: Install the Claude Code plugin and run `/open-code-review:delegate-review` on the next ai-daily-radar change so the review uses the already-signed-in Claude Code model (no separate OCR credentials).
Install the Codex plugin skills and have Codex run a review on a feature branch before you publish, saving the structured comments to a file.
Use `ocr scan --path ...` to audit an unfamiliar directory in a local project or a newly archived repo when there is no useful git diff.

Add a CI step that runs `ocr review` on the commit range for ai-daily-radar or other repos, writing comments you can triage without a long general-agent pass (the published benchmark uses about 1/9 the tokens of Claude Code for this task).
Connect the documented MCP server so the review agent can call external tools (for example an existing security or browser skill) during a review.

featured.reason: Plannotator (Apache-2.0) is a local browser-based review surface for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and other coding agents: annotate plans, specs, HTML artifacts and diffs, then send the comments back to the agent in one click. Includes Plannotator Inbox (plugins for Claude Code, Pi and OpenCode; MCP for other agents) and Codex skills (`$plannotator-review`, `$plannotator-annotate`, `$plannotator-last`). Rated 5. Caveat: the default installer auto-configures hooks/skills for detected agents and contacts GitHub Releases (and optionally npm); use `--minimal` if you only want the binary.
ideas: After a `--minimal` or full install, add the Claude Code plugin (`/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator@plannotator`) and review the next site-change plan in the annotation UI before letting the agent implement it.

Use `/plannotator-review` (or Codex `$plannotator-review`) on the local diff of ai-daily-radar so you can comment on the language-switch or mobile-background changes and send the markup back to the agent.
Run `plannotator inbox` so Claude Code, Codex and other agents can leave questions and HTML prototypes in one local window; reply when you are free without holding the session open.
Annotate a rendered HTML preview (for example a GitHub Pages build) with the visual review surface and send layout feedback to the agent instead of describing pixels in chat.

On the Mac mini terminal, try Herdr Annotate or `plannotator-tui` to review Markdown plans and agent replies without leaving the terminal; annotations are stored in the same Plannotator data directory.

news_highlights.title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Helsinki logician Jan von Plato had been transcribing Gödel's 1,009-page 1940s workbooks (much of it in obsolete Gabelsberger shorthand) at about a page a week. After feeding his transcriptions to Claude, he got a 650-page digest in days. The model extracted 663 candidate theorems; about 400 verified in Coq as stated and ~200 were repaired. A reconstructed near-proof of the independence of the axiom of choice also passed Coq, though historians still need to separate Gödel from the reconstruction.

news_highlights.title: MCP Is Dead Simple. And That's Exactly the Problem
news_highlights.why_it_matters: A widely discussed DEV.to piece argues that standing up an MCP server is easy, but production use still needs authorization, a human-in-the-loop for consequential writes, idempotency, and distrust of tool descriptions. In the demo, the agent filed the same HR complaint twice at different severities and ignored a DEMO ONLY header. Practical caution if you are wiring MCP servers into coding agents.

news_highlights.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
news_highlights.why_it_matters: On 13 Nov 2026, ggml-org cut llama.cpp and ggml to library v1.0.0 and committed to semantic versioning: major bumps for breaking changes to the public C API/ABI. That is a stability signal for local inference apps and packagers (Homebrew, conda-forge, Docker, Debian, Winget, XCFramework) that already depend on these interfaces.

news_highlights.title: After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models
news_highlights.why_it_matters: After 600 experiments on LeCun-linked LeWM, Haddy Alchaer found the published model's predictions on trained paths already match perfect simulator physics; the big gains came from planning, not retraining. Chaining 25-step subgoals and charging a cost for jumps in a latent memory graph lifted long-horizon Push-T success from 22% to 85%. Scoring the pusher visible in a goal image was also quietly tanking results.

news_highlights.title: Announcing Rust 1.100.0
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Rust 1.100.0 (12 Nov 2026) finally stabilizes the never type ! after a decade, lands the core Allocator API for custom allocators on Vec and Box, and adds DropGuard. Cargo also gets dependency cooldowns (global-min-publish-age) so newly published crates can sit out a review window before they enter a lockfile — a practical supply-chain control for everyday builds.
